Summary: Atomic child process for implementing one bounded .NET function, feature, or UI behavior with explicit design, test contract, code change, targeted validation, and handoff evidence.
ValueStatement: Keeps implementation work small enough for autonomous agents to complete and for managers to report blockers without reading raw execution threads.
InterfaceContractSummary: The parent slice supplies accepted scope, repository target, architecture constraints, and solution skeleton evidence; this subprocess returns changed files, test evidence, and residual risks.
GovernanceNotes: Detailed coding instructions belong in this subprocess, role skills, and step prompts. The dispatcher must remain generic and only orchestrate process state, assignments, and artifact contracts.
ChangeSummary: Adds a reusable implementation subprocess that can be nested under the default .NET development slice.
GovernancePolicySummary: The subprocess cannot close until the change set and focused validation evidence are attached and linked to the requested behavior.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Runtime truth stays in durable process runs, step runs, artifacts, and agent execution logs. Manager reports summarize those records without becoming a second source of truth.
OperatingModeSummary: Assisted autonomous execution with manager observation and explicit rework loops when evidence is incomplete.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Designed for small real local app changes that can be built and tested without manual coding assistance.
Metrics: Share of feature subprocesses completed without parent escalation.
Time blocked by missing scope, missing scaffold, missing tests, or provider/tool failures.
Share of runs where manager-directed rework resolved a blocker before escalation.
Risks: The feature scope is too broad and agents produce partial implementation evidence.
Agents modify product files without a focused validation contract.
Manager summaries drift from durable process artifacts instead of referencing them.
TailoringRules: Use one subprocess run per bounded function, endpoint, component, or feature behavior.

When a full deliverable parent scope already supplies product root, app archetype, architecture constraints, and validation hooks, derive the first reviewable MVP behavior instead of blocking only because the parent request is broader than one feature. The derived behavior must not be scaffold-only, app-shell-only, setup-only, naming-only, or build-only proof.
Split UI, persistence, and integration-heavy work into separate child runs when focused proof would otherwise become vague.
Managers may request missing artifacts or targeted repair from assigned agents before escalation, but must keep the dispatcher generic.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Coordinate the child implementation run, summarize progress and blockers, and request narrow unblock actions from assigned agents.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A manager-capable AI or human operator that can interpret process artifacts, execution attempts, and agent handoffs.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Confirm the implementation approach fits the repository architecture and does not split source of truth.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Architecture reviewer for source ownership, layering, and integration impact.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Make the minimal code change and produce a reviewable change-set summary.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A .NET-capable implementer with repository read/write and build/test tools.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Define and verify focused proof for the feature behavior.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A reviewer capable of evaluating targeted unit, integration, build, and browser evidence.

Steps.Title: Capture feature or function boundary
Steps.Subtitle: One behavior only
Steps.Notes: Restate the requested function or feature as one observable behavior with repository target, acceptance criteria, exclusions, and expected proof. If the parent request is a full app or broad deliverable, derive the first reviewable MVP behavior from upstream scope, architecture, setup evidence, product root, app archetype, and validation hooks, then record excluded follow-up behavior. The derived behavior must not be scaffold-only, app-shell-only, setup-only, naming-only, or build-only proof; it must contain an observable product-specific interaction. Reject only when no safe behavior can be chosen without inventing requirements.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Parent slice scope, repository or project target, existing solution evidence, and requested behavior.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Feature scope packet with acceptance criteria, exclusions, and proof expectations.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Bounded behavior statement, affected surface, assumptions, and excluded follow-up work.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Feature manager can narrow the requested behavior but cannot drop accepted parent criteria or downgrade the requested product to scaffold-only readiness.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when upstream evidence is contradictory, the product root/app archetype/validation boundary is missing, the selected behavior is scaffold/setup/app-shell/build-only work, or no single behavior can be selected without inventing requirements.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can keep parent and child evidence aligned.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature scope packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by implementation, validation, and parent process handoff.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must identify one behavior, acceptance criteria, exclusions, target repository surface, proof commands, and any broader parent-scope items intentionally deferred to follow-up slices.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature acceptance criteria
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by test contract and validation steps.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must be concrete enough that validation can pass or fail without interpreting intent.

Steps.Title: Decide implementation approach
Steps.Subtitle: Fit the local architecture
Steps.Notes: Identify existing patterns, canonical data ownership, UI/application/domain/infrastructure boundaries, required services, and the smallest file set likely to change.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Feature scope packet, acceptance criteria, repository structure, and parent architecture notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Implementation plan and architecture decision or explicit no-ADR rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Touched boundaries, intended file set, source-of-truth decision, and risks.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Feature architect can block or split the feature when ownership or layering is unclear.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block on unclear canonical ownership, missing scaffold, unsafe cross-layer leakage, scope requiring a separate subprocess, or artifact recovery when required decision evidence is missing or invalid before branch routing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an architect-capable reviewer familiar with .NET and Blazor layering.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature implementation plan
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by implementer, validator, and manager rework decisions.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name the intended change surface, architecture constraints, and proof strategy.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature architecture decision
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable when the feature changes canonical ownership, persistence, integration contracts, or UI architecture.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Required when the feature alters source-of-truth ownership or cross-layer contracts.

Steps.Title: Define focused validation contract
Steps.Subtitle: Proof before broad work
Steps.Notes: Plan the smallest reliable proof commands and browser checks needed for the accepted behavior. Do not execute build, test, launch, or browser tools in this step. For UI proof, require the later validation step to obtain a launch receipt such as workspace_dotnet_run and navigate only to the returned URL instead of a guessed localhost port.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Feature scope, acceptance criteria, and implementation plan.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Validation contract with required tests, commands, exit-code expectations, and UI proof when applicable.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Mapped acceptance criteria to test/proof actions and any known validation gaps.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Validation owner can require a narrower implementation or additional proof when the behavior cannot be validated deterministically.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when no focused validation route can be designed, acceptance criteria are missing and cannot be inferred, or artifact recovery is required for missing or invalid validation-contract evidence before branch routing. Missing launch/runtime tooling is a validation prerequisite to document for the later validation step, not a blocker for writing the contract.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a validation-capable reviewer that can interpret tests and browser proof.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature validation contract
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by implementation, targeted validation, and parent QA.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must list focused test/build/browser proof commands and map each proof item to acceptance criteria.

Steps.Title: Implement the .NET feature or function
Steps.Subtitle: Minimal code path
Steps.Notes: Make the smallest production and test changes that satisfy the validation contract. Follow existing project conventions, keep state changes explicit, and avoid introducing fallback behavior that hides errors. Keep generated tests deterministic and bounded: avoid loops that depend only on mutable product state without a maximum iteration guard and an assertion that each state transition succeeded. Use a workspace_dotnet_test timeout of 300 seconds or less for focused generated-app tests unless a current diagnostic proves the test suite needs more time. This implementation step does not own runtime launch, browser navigation, screenshots, or viewport proof; those belong to targeted-validation because this step lacks LaunchRuntime and CaptureRuntimeProof. Do not block this step only because browser proof is missing when code changes, build, and focused tests are complete.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Feature scope, acceptance criteria, implementation plan, validation contract, and solution skeleton evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Reviewable code change with touched-file inventory and implementation rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Changed files, behavior implemented, tests added or updated, assumptions, and risks.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Feature implementer can choose local implementation details but cannot widen behavior beyond the scope packet.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block on missing dependencies, missing target files, unsafe architecture mismatch, or validation contract gaps instead of guessing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a .NET-capable implementer with repository write and build/test tools.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature implementation change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by validation, peer review, and parent handoff.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include changed files, behavioral intent, tests touched, and known risks.

Steps.Title: Run focused validation
Steps.Subtitle: Pass or request rework
Steps.Notes: Run the agreed validation commands and browser proof. Keep focused validation bounded: use a workspace_dotnet_test timeout of 300 seconds or less for generated or focused tests unless a current diagnostic proves the test suite needs more time. If validation hangs or times out, record the command and timeout as failing proof and choose the feature-repair-required branch instead of waiting on a broad unbounded run. For UI proof, launch or verify the app first, use the returned URL, then collect browser snapshot, console messages, and screenshot. If proof fails because an artifact is missing, the app cannot launch, or the implementation is incomplete, choose feature-repair-required and route the defect to the owning implementation role. Use blocked status only for an unrecoverable environment, permission, or process-contract problem that cannot be repaired inside this subprocess.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Feature change set and validation contract.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Focused validation evidence plus an explicit feature-accepted or feature-repair-required branch.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Commands, exit codes, relevant logs, screenshots for UI, and acceptance-criteria mapping.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Validation owner can accept proof or route targeted rework, but cannot mutate product files in this step.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Select feature-repair-required for failing proof, missing artifacts, app launch failures, incomplete implementation, or evidence that does not map to the accepted behavior. Block only when repair cannot be attempted because the environment, permissions, or process contract is unavailable.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a reviewer capable of running and interpreting the required proof.
Rebind only to a manager that can request targeted rework before escalation.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature test evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent QA and release readiness.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include commands, exit codes, relevant output, UI proof when applicable, and unresolved gaps.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Feature accepted
BranchOutcomes.Description: Focused validation evidence satisfies the accepted behavior and the feature can be handed to the parent process.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Feature repair required
BranchOutcomes.Description: Focused validation found a concrete defect, failed proof, missing artifact, launch failure, or implementation gap that the implementer must repair.

Steps.Title: Hand off feature implementation
Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready accepted result
Steps.Notes: Summarize the initially accepted feature implementation path: what changed, what passed, what remains risky, and whether the parent process should continue, request another subprocess, or escalate.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Feature scope, change set, and accepted validation evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent-ready handoff packet with status, blockers, residual risks, and next recommendation.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Implementation summary, validation result, open issues, and explicit parent next action.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Feature manager can close only when the feature-accepted branch was selected and required evidence exists.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close on the initial path when validation selected repair-required, required artifacts are missing, or the parent cannot determine the next action.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can produce parent-ready reports.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature implementation handoff packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent implementation slice, peer review, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must summarize change, validation result, blockers, risks, and parent next action.

Steps.Title: Repair .NET focused validation findings
Steps.Subtitle: Targeted implementation rework
Steps.Notes: Repair only the concrete defects, failed proof, launch issue, or missing artifacts identified by targeted validation. Stay inside the accepted feature scope and rerun the smallest useful validation command before handing back to QA recheck.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Feature change set, focused validation evidence, and feature-repair-required disposition.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Focused repair change set and validation notes ready for recheck.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Repaired defect, changed files, rerun command output when available, and remaining risk.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Feature implementer owns product changes; QA may clarify failing evidence without mutating product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not broaden the feature scope. Escalate if the requested repair requires a new behavior, architecture change, missing permission, or unavailable tool.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a .NET-capable implementer with repository write and build/test tools.
QA can clarify the failing proof without taking ownership of product changes.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature repair change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by recheck, parent QA, and release readiness.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name the failing proof addressed, changed files, rerun validation, and unresolved risk.

Steps.Title: Re-run focused validation after repair
Steps.Subtitle: Repair proof
Steps.Notes: Re-run the failing proof and the smallest regression commands needed to verify the repair. Select feature-accepted only when the repaired evidence satisfies the accepted behavior. Select feature-repair-escalation when the same blocker remains, a new release-blocking issue appears, or another repair would exceed the subprocess scope.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Original validation failure, repair change set, and validation contract.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Recheck evidence plus an explicit feature-accepted or feature-repair-escalation branch.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Rerun commands, exit codes, browser proof when applicable, and acceptance-criteria mapping after repair.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Validation owner can accept repaired evidence or escalate unresolved repair findings; QA still does not mutate product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Select feature-repair-escalation when proof remains failing, missing, detached, or unmapped after repair. Block only for environment, permission, or process-contract failures that prevent recheck execution.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a reviewer capable of rerunning and interpreting the required proof.
Implementation owner reviews remaining findings before parent escalation.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature repair recheck evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent QA and release readiness.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include rerun commands, exit codes, relevant output, UI proof when applicable, and unresolved gaps after repair.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Feature accepted
BranchOutcomes.Description: Repaired focused validation evidence satisfies the accepted behavior and the feature can be handed to the parent process.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Feature repair escalation
BranchOutcomes.Description: Repaired validation still has release-blocking proof gaps or defects that require parent escalation or a new subprocess scope.

Steps.Title: Hand off repaired feature implementation
Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready repaired result
Steps.Notes: Summarize the repaired accepted path: original failure, repair, recheck evidence, remaining risks, and whether the parent process should continue.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Feature scope, original change set, repair change set, and accepted recheck evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent-ready repaired handoff packet with status, blockers, residual risks, and next recommendation.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Implementation summary, repair summary, validation result, open issues, and explicit parent next action.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Feature manager can close only when the repaired feature-accepted branch was selected and required evidence exists.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close when repaired validation selected escalation, required artifacts are missing, or the parent cannot determine the next action.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can produce parent-ready reports.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Repaired feature implementation handoff packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent implementation slice, peer review, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must summarize original change, repair change, validation result, blockers, risks, and parent next action.

Steps.Title: Escalate unresolved feature repair
Steps.Subtitle: Parent no-go packet
Steps.Notes: Record the unresolved repair findings and make the parent no-go recommendation explicit instead of closing the child as accepted.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Original validation failure, repair change set, and failed recheck evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent escalation packet with unresolved defects, proof gaps, risks, and recommended next action.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Unresolved blocker list, failing proof references, attempted repair, and parent escalation recommendation.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Feature manager can escalate unresolved repair findings but cannot present the feature as accepted.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not continue to parent-ready accepted handoff while repaired validation remains unresolved.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can produce no-go reports.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Feature repair escalation packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent implementation slice, incident review, and future repair planning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must summarize unresolved findings, attempted repair, failing proof, no-go rationale, and required next scope.
